story.iWant: my recordings to automatically appear in the media library and timeline after stopping
story.soThat: I can immediately start editing without manual import steps
story.tasks: - Implement auto-import trigger (AC: 1) - Integrate with media library (AC: 2, 3) - Implement screen-only timeline placement (AC: 4) - Implement webcam-only timeline placement (AC: 5) - Implement PiP timeline placement (AC: 6, 7) - Calculate PiP positioning (AC: 7) - Implement timeline scroll/adjustment (AC: 8) - Implement success notification (AC: 9) - Ensure performance requirements (AC: 10) - Implement error handling (AC: 11) - Implement comprehensive logging (AC: 12) - Update existing stores (AC: 1, 4, 5, 6) - Write integration tests - Manual testing with real recordings

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: After recording stops, output files automatically imported to media library
Media library generates thumbnails for recorded files (first frame)
Recorded files appear in media library with metadata (filename, duration, resolution)
Screen-only recording: clip automatically placed on Timeline Track 1
Webcam-only recording: clip automatically placed on Timeline Track 2 (overlay track)
PiP recording: both clips placed simultaneously (screen → Track 1, webcam → Track 2)
Webcam clips on Track 2 positioned bottom-right at 20% size (PiP positioning)
Timeline automatically scrolls/adjusts to show newly added clips
Success notification displayed: "Recording added to timeline" with recording duration
All auto-import steps complete within 5 seconds of recording stop (NFR)
Error handling for import failures with user-friendly messages
Logging for all auto-import operations with [Recording] prefix

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Steps 10-13 in each workflow: auto-import files to media library, generate thumbnails, auto-place on timeline tracks, display success notification. Screen→Track 1, Webcam→Track 2.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Media Library Integration uses existing mediaStore.addFile() API. Timeline Integration uses existing timelineStore.addClipToTrack() API. Requires multi-track support from Epic 4.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Webcam position: bottom-right, size: 20% (0.2), shape: circular. Applied in timeline/preview, NOT during recording.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Auto-Import Speed: Recorded files must appear in media library within 5 seconds of recording stop. Timeline Placement must complete instantly (<500ms).

doc.title: Decision Architecture
doc.snippet: Multi-track timeline support with Track 1 (main) and Track 2 (overlay). VideoCanvas for multi-track compositing with overlay positioning.

artifact.reason: Media library state management - addFile() method used for importing recorded files with metadata
Timeline state management - addClipToTrack() method for placing clips on specific tracks with positioning metadata
Recording state with stopRecording action - needs to trigger auto-import after IPC returns output files
Multi-track compositing component - needs to apply circular clip-path and positioning for webcam overlay clips

node.package: State management for media, timeline, and recording stores

constraints.constraint: Two-track placement inherited from Epic 4.1 - multi-track timeline must already exist
Screen recordings always go to Track 1 (main/background track)
Webcam recordings always go to Track 2 (overlay track)
Webcam overlay positioning: bottom-right corner, 20% of screen dimensions
Webcam shape: circular (applied via CSS clip-path or canvas)
Positioning stored in clip metadata, applied by VideoCanvas
Auto-import happens immediately after stopRecording IPC returns
Thumbnail generation can be asynchronous (doesn't block timeline placement)
All auto-import steps must complete within 5 seconds total (NFR)
For PiP: both clips must start at same timeline position (synchronized)

interface.name: ClipData with overlay positioning

tests.standards: Integration tests with mocked stores and IPC. Test track assignment logic for each recording mode. Test PiP positioning calculations with various screen resolutions. Manual testing critical for end-to-end flow. Measure performance with console.time() at each step.

ideas.idea: Test stopRecording triggers autoImportRecordings with output files
Mock thumbnail service, verify thumbnail generation called for each file
Test mediaStore.addFile called with correct metadata (filename, duration, resolution)
Test screen-only recording adds clip to Track 1
Test webcam-only recording adds clip to Track 2
Test PiP recording adds screen to Track 1 AND webcam to Track 2

Test positioning for different resolutions: 1280x720 screen → webcam at correct bottom-right 20%
Test timeline scrolls/adjusts viewport after clip placement
Test success notification displayed with correct message and duration
Measure total time from stopRecording to timeline visible (<5s)
Test error handling: file not found, thumbnail fails, timeline placement fails
Verify all logs include [Recording] prefix and relevant context
